page.notes: Large public news publication. Core content is strongly server-rendered, with substantial client-side advertising, consent, and interactive enhancement.

paths.description: Homepage: primary discovery surface and global chrome. Represents the broad news feed and consent entry state.
Science article: representative long-form detail template and primary reading journey.
Stock-market liveblog: representative frequently updated interactive content template.
Deliberately missing route: representative HTTP/navigation recovery state.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance and byte size to the default capture, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Animations continue while reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirmed the media query matched but found seven running animations with 1–2 second durations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use prefers-reduced-motion to remove non-essential animation and auto-advance, not merely declare a rule.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation was found.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found neither prefers-contrast nor forced-colors handling; Lighthouse also found 28 low-contrast elements on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast treatments that preserve control boundaries and readable text.

findings.summary: Page and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The full CSS probe found no view-transition rules or declarations across the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin article and section navigation with cross-document View Transitions and a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not expose scroll-state-aware behavior.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll-state container query or animation timeline despite a 24,163px homepage and persistent navigation chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight progress affordance to orient readers on long feeds and articles.

findings.summary: Large menus and overlays are manually positioned rather than anchored.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found a large city overlay but no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions for menus and tooltips near viewport edges.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures all editorial content on every tested content template.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots of the homepage, section, article, and liveblog all open with a near/full-viewport consent layer over the primary content.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer a compact, non-blocking consent surface where legally possible and ensure immediate, reliable dismissal.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is implemented as custom div-based dialog chrome.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe identifies role=dialog divs and a large fixed div, but no native dialog element for the modal flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic dialog for the modal consent flow with native focus management, escape behavior, and explicit close semantics.

findings.summary: The news feed is crowded by controls, promotional chrome, and ad infrastructure.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe counted 1,995 controls and the mobile document is 24,163px tall; the first content view is additionally hidden by consent UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated controls and promotional modules, prioritize headlines and article content, and defer low-value widgets.

findings.summary: No component-level container-query adaptation was found.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules across a homepage with many reused card and navigation components.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable cards and modules while retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.guidanceId: touch target size hover fallback pointer input focus-visible
findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch target support are weak.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the first visible link computed to outline:none; the probe counted 453 controls below 24px in one dimension, and Lighthouse found 8 article target-size failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge/space actionable targets to at least WCAG target-size expectations.

findings.summary: Rejecting tracking can leave a blank modal that still blocks the page.
findings.evidence: After activating “Do not consent” and waiting 3 seconds, the captured homepage remained dimmed behind a completely blank blocking panel.
findings.suggestedFix: Make both consent outcomes deterministic and atomic: close the modal, restore focus, and reveal content after state persistence succeeds or show an actionable retry error.

findings.guidanceId: loading empty error success retry undo cancel state
findings.summary: The failed consent transition has no state explanation or recovery action.
findings.evidence: The post-rejection screenshot shows an empty white panel with no loading indicator, error message, close, retry, or back action.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose an accessible loading state with a short timeout, then an error message and retry/continue-without-tracking recovery.

findings.summary: Synthetic mobile performance is outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 10.3s, CLS 0.257 and TBT 350ms; the article measured LCP 5.5s, TBT 410ms and 31.2s time to interactive.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the true LCP element, reserve late content space, and reduce startup JavaScript and third-party work.

findings.guidanceId: prevent layout shift reserve space CLS aspect-ratio
findings.summary: The homepage shifts substantially during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.257 and identified layout-shift culprits; the images audit found all 100 homepage images missing a complete width/height pair.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image, ad, and consent UI space with width/height or aspect-ratio and avoid late insertion above existing content.

findings.summary: Heavy script work delays interactivity.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 350–410ms TBT and 13.2–31.2s time to interactive, while the HAR recorded 77 scripts totaling 2.28MB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, split long tasks, and schedule low-value work after interaction readiness.

findings.summary: The homepage delivers an excessive request and byte payload.
findings.evidence: HAR: 187 requests and 4.09MB transferred, including 2.28MB scripts; 178 requests and 3.84MB were classified off the main origin. Confirmed candidate ad scripts are async, so the issue is volume and dependency cost rather than parser blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Set budgets, delay ad/analytics stacks until consent and idle/interaction, compress text, and improve caching.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the load.
findings.evidence: The HAR largest scripts include Taboola 330KB, Google ad code 202KB, gtag 177KB, prebid 147KB and GTM 131KB before accounting for their follow-on requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate vendors and conditionally load each third-party only when the corresponding feature and consent state require it.

findings.summary: The homepage has many unnamed images and an unlabeled search field.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 51 of 100 homepage images without alt; the DOM probe found the text search input had zero associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images concise alt text, mark decorative images empty-alt, and provide the search input an explicit accessible label.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 28 homepage contrast failures and 3 article failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to meet WCAG AA in default, hover, focus, disabled, and consent states.

findings.summary: Heading structure and focus visibility are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage has multiple H1s including consent headings, Lighthouse found article heading-order failures, and the first focused link computed with no outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one content H1 per page, nest headings sequentially, and provide persistent :focus-visible styles in reading order.

findings.summary: The viewport restricts zoom and several targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: The viewport declares maximum-scale=1; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport and found 8 target-size failures on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale, allow user zoom, and enlarge/space touch targets.

findings.summary: Both tested templates log browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console on both the homepage and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the recorded resource/runtime errors and add production error monitoring with release ownership.

findings.summary: Document and image hygiene is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The article failed charset placement and image aspect-ratio checks; the image audits found 100/100 homepage and 17/18 article images missing complete dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Place charset early in head, preserve intrinsic image aspect ratios, and emit width and height for every content image.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and DevTools issues remain on the article template.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated API warning and failed inspector-issues on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the deprecated API and resolve the concrete Issues-panel reports before release.

findings.guidanceId: crawlable links viewport meta robots descriptive link text
findings.summary: Mobile and link semantics undermine otherwise strong discoverability.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 25 non-descriptive homepage links and failed the zoom-restricting viewport; robots permits core content and raw HTML coverage remains high.
findings.suggestedFix: Use descriptive anchor text/accessibility names and remove maximum-scale from the viewport.

findings.summary: Cookie and header hardening is incomplete.
findings.evidence: All 17 observed cookies were reported insecure; many use SameSite=None, while nosniff is missing and HSTS lasts only one day. HTTPS, CSP and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every HTTPS cookie, minimize SameSite=None, add nosniff, and use a long-lived HSTS policy after rollout validation.

findings.summary: The page contacts an unusually broad tracking and advertising ecosystem before a consent choice.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 39 third-party origins and 11 known tracker endpoints; HAR classified 178/187 requests and 3.84MB off the main origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to no non-essential vendor requests before consent, reduce vendors, and document purpose/retention for each remaining endpoint.

findings.summary: Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options; CSP frame-ancestors and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strict, tested Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy headers and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

findings.summary: The consent overlay enters a broken persistent top-layer state.
findings.evidence: After rejection the blocking panel remains blank over live content, demonstrating fragile asynchronous overlay state.
findings.suggestedFix: Sequence consent persistence and dismissal, restore focus, and provide timeout/error recovery.

findings.summary: Images are broadly oversized, dimensionless, and not responsive.
findings.evidence: Homepage: 75/100 oversized, 92 missing srcset, 97 below-fold images not lazy, and 100 missing complete dimensions; article: 14/18 oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive srcset/sizes, use modern formats where supported, lazy-load below-fold media, and emit dimensions.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics work is disproportionate to initial reader value.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 187 requests, 77 scripts, 27 fetch/XHR requests, and large analytics/ad/WASM dependencies while a consent wall blocks reading.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not start non-essential work before consent; defer, batch, and cancel background work when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party bytes consume nearly the entire transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR classified 3.84MB of 4.09MB transferred and 178 of 187 requests off the main origin; trackers found 39 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish a third-party byte/request budget and remove or lazy-load vendors that do not deliver measurable reader value.

findings.summary: The public news experience exposes content but no structured agent capability layer.
findings.evidence: Discoverability is strong (90–98% raw HTML coverage), but Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 0.49 on home and 0.67 on article and reported llms.txt guidance failures; no WebMCP registration was found in the DOM probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep server-rendered content and add a carefully scoped machine-readable policy/capability surface only for safe read/search actions.
